clinician.final_diagnosis: Chronic kidney disease due to diabetic nephropathy with acute exacerbation primarily caused by IgG4-related ureteral obstruction and IgG4-related tubulointerstitial nephritis (IgG4-TIN)
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 87-year-old male with longstanding diabetes and chronic kidney disease presented with anorexia, nausea, and acute worsening renal function (creatinine 428 μmol/L). Imaging revealed a right ureter mass causing obstruction. Biopsy of the ureteral orifice showed fibrous tissue infiltrated by IgG4-positive plasma cells. Renal biopsy demonstrated diabetic nephropathy features alongside abundant IgG4-positive cells and storiform fibrosis consistent with IgG4-TIN. Placement of a double-J stent decreased obstruction and creatinine improved to 279 μmol/L. Corticosteroid therapy resulted in further reduction of creatinine to 196 μmol/L and lowered IgG4 levels. One year follow-up showed sustained renal function stability and low IgG4 with tapering steroids, confirming diagnosis and effective treatment.
